clue.text: Sulky nag turns up to repeat it all over again

indicators.note: in a down clue the horse's name is read from the bottom upwards, so it turns up

parts.note: a pacer is a harness-racing horse that pulls a sulky, a light two-wheeled cart

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered old horse keeps coming back to do the same thing again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sulky' looks like a mood but is the light cart of harness racing; its horse is a PACER, which written upwards gives the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapitulate a summary is to go over the main points a second time.

clue.text: Address for delivery

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience
the manner or style in which someone talks

explanation.surface: A note on where a parcel should be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk to an audience, and delivery can mean a manner of talking, as in clear diction.

clue.text: Turkey was, understand ably, so treated by the Treaty of Berlin

definitions.text: Turkey was, understand ably, so treated by the Treaty of Berlin

parts.words: Turkey was, understand ably, so treated by the Treaty of Berlin
parts.note: the bird at a Christmas table is sliced for serving, and the Ottoman state lost much territory when the 1878 Berlin settlement divided its lands

explanation.surface: A history note on how the 1878 Congress of Berlin dealt with the Ottoman Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Treaty of Berlin (1878) stripped Ottoman Turkey of Balkan provinces; the turkey of the table gets the same treatment from a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sliced into portions describes both a roast bird and a nation whose territory was divided among powers.

clue.text: Accumulate a bill while on Mediterranean tourist island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
Crete is the large Greek island popular with holidaymakers

explanation.surface: Running up a tab while holidaying on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by gradual addition, building up layer upon layer.

clue.text: Absolutely no idea for this one!

definitions.text: Absolutely no idea for this one!

parts.words: Absolutely no idea for this one!
parts.note: a solver's cry of total bafflement, while also hinting that this clue offers no hint at all

explanation.surface: A stumped solver's exasperated remark about a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses complete ignorance, and the self-referential clue jokes that it gives the solver no help.

clue.text: Ted went to bed

definitions.meaning: to ted is to spread and toss cut grass so it dries
retired for the night, the slang phrase being the same in past and present

explanation.surface: A man named Ted retired for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ted' looks like a man's name, but to ted is a farming verb: to spread mown grass out to dry, which is a playful way of striking at fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedding is turning and scattering cut grass, a literal assault on fodder, and the idiom means retired to sleep.

clue.text: Guard against losing time

parts.note: read as staying alert on sentry duty, or as holding on to your timepiece so it is not lost

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful not to fall behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries keep vigil, and someone who holds on to their wristwatch has not lost the thing that tells the hour.

clue.text: Amusing publication for the young

definitions.meaning: funny, making people laugh
a children's magazine of cartoon strips

explanation.surface: A description of an entertaining children's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something funny can be called this, and it is also a cartoon-strip magazine aimed at children.

clue.text: Pacific paradise lies in ruin

indicators.note: something in ruin is wrecked and broken up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tropical paradise has fallen into decay.
explanation.definitionFit: A South Sea island is a classic image of a tropical paradise in the Pacific.

clue.text: Invitation to bowler hatted company speculator?

definitions.text: Invitation to bowler hatted company speculator?

parts.words: Invitation to bowler hatted company speculator?
parts.note: a captain inviting a cricket bowler to bowl the next set of six balls, and a City financier in a bowler hat buying up a firm

explanation.surface: A City gent in a bowler hat is being invited into a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the captain tells a bowler to bowl the next over; in the City a bowler-hatted speculator acquires control of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a cricket captain's instruction and the term for buying control of a firm.

clue.text: Sea air provided by ramshackle chalet

definitions.meaning: a sailors' work song, air meaning tune
a rough tumbledown hut

explanation.surface: Breezy coastal air drifting through a tumbledown holiday hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailors' work song is a sea air, and a crude hut or shack is also called by the same word.

clue.text: African state producing tea and date

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A country known for its tea and dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Band music for the Royal Horse Guards

definitions.meaning: a melancholy genre of music played by a band
the regiment's nickname, from their blue uniforms

explanation.surface: A note on what a cavalry regiment's band plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Horse Guards were nicknamed after their blue tunics; they merged into the Blues and Royals, a British Household Cavalry regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A melancholy music genre from the American South shares its name with the nickname of a British cavalry regiment.

clue.text: Junior seat leads to senior professorial post

definitions.meaning: a tall seat for a baby at mealtimes
an elevated academic chair, chair meaning professorship

explanation.surface: Progress from a child's seat at the table to a top university position.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat for toddlers at meals, and also an elevated academic chair, a senior professorship.

clue.text: Well supplied fuel carrier

parts.note: something fed from a well that conveys fuel, rather than a carrier that is well stocked

explanation.surface: A tanker or truck that is amply stocked with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well supplied' looks like 'amply stocked', but it means supplied from a well: crude petroleum from a borehole goes through this conduit.
explanation.definitionFit: A conduit carrying petroleum from a borehole is fed by a well and transports fuel.

clue.text: Blackout suffered by demoted dictator

definitions.meaning: a loss of electricity supply
a reduction in authority, read literally

explanation.surface: A deposed tyrant's palace is left without electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss of electricity supply causes a blackout, and a demoted tyrant has had his authority reduced.

clue.text: Gunners store of ammunition

definitions.meaning: nickname of a north London football club
a depot of weapons and munitions

explanation.surface: Artillerymen guarding a munitions depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal, the north London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunners is the nickname of a London football club, and the same word means a weapons depot.

clue.text: Left in even though fully extended

definitions.text: Left in even though fully extended

parts.words: Left in even though fully extended
parts.note: swapping each word of the first phrase for its opposite gives a phrase meaning completely or all the way

explanation.surface: Something stayed inside despite being stretched as far as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the opposites of 'Left' and 'in' to get the phrase, which also means completely or fully.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means completely, all the way, and is the word-by-word opposite of left in.

clue.text: Main Mosaic order that effected Israel's flight from Egypt

definitions.text: Main Mosaic order that effected Israel's flight from Egypt

parts.words: Main Mosaic order that effected Israel's flight from Egypt
parts.note: the main is an old word for the ocean, and the command associated with Moses parted the Red Sea for the Israelites

explanation.surface: A biblical account of the instruction from Moses that let the Israelites escape Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' means the ocean, and 'Mosaic' means of Moses, not tiled; in Exodus the Red Sea parted for the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the ocean far from land, and the phrase is also the command to part the waters.

clue.text: Attended but caused embarrassment

definitions.meaning: turned up, arrived
exposed someone, made them look bad

explanation.surface: Someone came along but made everyone uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning up somewhere means attending it, and exposing someone's failings embarrasses them.

clue.text: Transvestite habit exposed by old penny dreadful?

parts.note: D stood for the pre-decimal British penny, from the Latin denarius
a penny dreadful was a cheap sensational paper, and a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A Victorian penny dreadful scandalously exposing a cross-dresser's habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' means clothing, as a nun wears one, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's clothing worn by a man, especially a performer, is called this; habit here means attire.

clue.text: Gun pointed at an opening in the wall

parts.note: gat is old gangster slang for a pistol
E is a point of the compass, so pointed suggests the letter E

explanation.surface: A gun aimed at a hole in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged barrier closing a gap in a wall or fence is a gate.

clue.text: Hard cheese is not good enough

definitions.meaning: British slang for bad luck, said without sympathy
falling short, unacceptable

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tough cheese falls short of standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck, often said without much sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is a British expression of unsympathetic commiseration, and the phrase also means falling short.

clue.text: Everybody has to gamble when they play it

definitions.text: Everybody has to gamble when they play it

parts.note: the lot means everyone, the whole group

explanation.surface: Everyone must take a chance when playing a game of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lottery-style game of chance in which players gamble on numbers drawn.

clue.text: Routine task leading to a nervous complaint

indicators.note: the first piece comes before, or leads to, the second

parts.note: a chore is a dull everyday job

explanation.surface: Endless housework is driving someone into nervous illness.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a neurological disorder causing jerky involuntary movements, as in Huntington's.

clue.text: Cooler can't be all that good

definitions.meaning: less warm
mediocre, unimpressive

explanation.surface: A refrigerator that seems not to work very well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less warm is cooler, and a mediocre thing is said to be unimpressive.

clue.text: Take notice, but don't retire

definitions.meaning: become suddenly alert
stay awake instead of going to bed

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention rather than go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To become alert is to take notice, and to stay awake late instead of going to bed is the same phrase.

clue.text: Girl coming out only to be taunted gets worked up

indicators.note: letters worked up are agitated and stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl at her coming-out ball gets upset at being mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A society girl making her first formal appearance at a ball is said to come out.
